title: §01-007: Maven Project Structure & JUnit 5 Testing
description: Standard directory layout, build lifecycle phases, dependency scopes, JUnit 5 Jupiter architecture, and assertions.

cards.question: In the Apache Maven standard directory layout, where should production Java source files be located?
cards.explanation: Convention over configuration: Maven strictly expects production Java source files in `src/main/java`, application resources in `src/main/resources`, unit test sources in `src/test/java`, and test resources in `src/test/resources`.
cards.codeSnippet:
my-project/
├── pom.xml
└── src/
    ├── main/
    │   ├── java/        <- Production Java source code
    │   └── resources/   <- Production config (application.yml)
    └── test/
        ├── java/        <- Test Java source code
        └── resources/   <- Test fixtures
cards.pitfall: Placing resource files (like XML, JSON, or properties) inside `src/main/java` without explicit `<resources>` filters in `pom.xml` means Maven will ignore them and not copy them to `target/classes`.
cards.citation: Introduction to Maven (Jenkins) / Create an Enterprise-Level Test Automation Framework (Das) Ch. 2

cards.question: When running the command `mvn package`, which phase executes immediately before `package` in the default build lifecycle?
cards.explanation: The default lifecycle phases execute sequentially: `validate` -> `compile` -> `test` -> `package` -> `verify` -> `install` -> `deploy`. When you invoke `mvn package`, Maven automatically runs all prior phases (including compiling code and executing unit tests).
cards.codeSnippet:
% mvn package
[INFO] --- maven-resources-plugin: resources ---
[INFO] --- maven-compiler-plugin: compile ---
[INFO] --- maven-surefire-plugin: test ---
[INFO] --- maven-jar-plugin: jar (package) ---
cards.pitfall: Running `mvn package -DskipTests` bypasses test execution, which risks packaging broken code into deployable artifacts.

cards.question: Which dependency `<scope>` should be declared for testing libraries (like JUnit 5 or Mockito) so they are excluded from the packaged production JAR/WAR?
cards.explanation: `test` scope dependencies are available only for test compilation and test execution. They are not transitive and are never bundled into the production package created by `mvn package`.
cards.pitfall: Omitting the `<scope>test</scope>` tag defaults the dependency to `compile` scope, needlessly bloating production JAR/WAR files with test frameworks.

cards.question: What is the primary function of the `<dependencyManagement>` section in a parent Maven POM?

options.text: It immediately downloads and includes all declared artifacts in every child project.
It defines and centralizes dependency versions and configurations without actually adding them to the dependency tree until child POMs reference them.
It deletes conflicting JARs from the local `.m2` repository.
It converts Maven projects to Gradle builds.

cards.explanation: `<dependencyManagement>` is a lookup table for dependency versions. Child modules inherit these versions and only need to specify `<groupId>` and `<artifactId>`, avoiding version fragmentation across multi-module enterprise repositories.
cards.codeSnippet:
<!-- In Parent POM: -->
<dependencyManagement>
    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
            <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
            <version>2.0.12</version>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>
</dependencyManagement>

<!-- In Child POM (no version required): -->
<dependencies>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
        <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
    </dependency>
</dependencies>
cards.pitfall: Adding dependencies directly under `<dependencies>` in a parent POM forces every single child module to inherit that dependency, even if they don't need it.

cards.question: What is the core API package and annotation used to declare a test method in JUnit 5 (Jupiter)?
cards.explanation: JUnit 5 is modularized into Jupiter (API & Engine), Vintage (JUnit 3/4 runner), and Platform. Test annotations reside in `org.junit.jupiter.api.*`. Methods annotated with `@Test` in JUnit 5 do not need to be `public` (package-private is preferred).
cards.pitfall: Accidentally importing `org.junit.Test` (JUnit 4) instead of `org.junit.jupiter.api.Test` in a JUnit 5 project will cause tests to be skipped unless the Vintage engine is present.
cards.citation: Complete Guide to Java Testing with JUnit 5 & Mockito (van Putten)

cards.question: Why should `assertAll()` be preferred over multiple sequential `assertEquals()` statements when validating multiple properties on an object?

options.text: `assertAll()` executes the assertions in separate OS processes for speed.
Sequential assertions fail-fast on the first failure (hiding subsequent failures), whereas `assertAll` executes all assertions and reports all failures together.

cards.explanation: If you have 4 sequential assertions and the 1st fails, the remaining 3 are never executed, creating a tedious game of whack-a-mole during debugging. `assertAll()` accepts lambdas, executes all assertions regardless of failures, and prints a comprehensive consolidated failure report.
cards.pitfall: Don't place dependencies between assertions inside `assertAll()`. If assertion 2 depends on assertion 1 not being null, use an explicit initial check.
cards.citation: JUnit 5 User Guide §Assertions / Test Automation Framework (Das) Ch. 3

cards.question: How should an expected exception be verified in JUnit 5?

options.text: Wrapping the code in a manual `try-catch` with a `fail()` call.

cards.explanation: JUnit 5 deprecated the JUnit 4 `@Test(expected = ...)` attribute in favor of `assertThrows()`. It takes the expected exception class and an executable lambda, and returns the caught exception instance so you can further assert on its message or error codes.
cards.pitfall: `assertThrows` asserts on exact type or subclasses. If the method throws a different exception or no exception at all, the assertion fails.

cards.question: What lifecycle hook in JUnit 5 executes once before all test methods in a class, and what requirement does it have by default?

options.text: `@BeforeAll`, and it must be annotated on a `static` method by default.
`@SetupClass`, and it must return a boolean.
`@PreTest`, and it must take an `ApplicationContext` argument.

cards.explanation: `@BeforeAll` runs once before any `@Test` methods execute in the test class. Under the default lifecycle (`Lifecycle.PER_METHOD`), the test class instance is recreated for each test method; hence `@BeforeAll` methods must be `static` unless `@TestInstance(Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)` is configured.
cards.pitfall: Declaring a non-static `@BeforeAll` method without `@TestInstance(Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)` will throw a JUnitConfigurationException at runtime.
